meta.storyTitle: Build and sign Linux x86-64 daemon artifacts

override.reason: User explicitly approved this S1 LLD with a manual review override while automated design review is broken. Critical self-review checked exact signed origin, independent qualification verification, signing sequence concurrency and rollback boundaries. Structure and signing diagram were verified.

summary.prose: This story packages the existing daemon and its native dependencies for Ubuntu 24.04 amd64. It defines the manifest and verification rules that allow qualification and release signing to authenticate the same bytes. Existing Darwin artifacts keep their formats.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Add a versioned Linux x86-64 bundle and target-specific publication path. Reuse signed manifest verification and safe staging primitives where compatible, and retain distinct development, qualification and production trust. Use a user-scoped Linux lifecycle coordinator with retained process identity and an offline recoverable selector.

ownedContracts.name: Linux artifact identity and trust
ownedContracts.purpose: S1 defines the signed subject and host compatibility envelope used by S2 admission and S3 promotion. One build origin supplies one exact manifest and archive for a target and channel. Qualification, development and production signature grants stay separate and cannot satisfy one another. LinuxReleaseIdentity is the verified envelope. The controller calculates manifestSha256 from the exact manifest bytes and compares it to the protected evidence. The digest is external to the signed manifest payload.

ownedContracts.name: Target-bound release qualification
ownedContracts.purpose: S1 owns the subject binding used by the qualification signer, installer and publication consumer. Each promotion requires complete evidence for one exact target subject and the applicable compatibility pair. S3 defines the runner, validates and records the local evidence, and authorizes exact-byte promotion. Promotion validates required test IDs and outcomes against independently authenticated release-owner evidence. The artifact build cannot issue this evidence. Each compatibility proof binds exact candidate and predecessor fingerprints plus the covered state contract.
ownedContracts.interfaceSketch:
interface QualificationSubject { target: ReleaseTarget; manifestSha256: string; archiveSha256: string; origin: CandidateOrigin; channel: string; }
interface QualificationEvidenceRef { subject: QualificationSubject; deviceProfileDigest: string; testEvidenceDigests: readonly string[]; predecessorEvidenceId?: string; }

boundary.internal: Linux packaging, versioned metadata and protected signing primitives. Use controlled fixtures for verifier and policy tests so implementing S1 does not require live publication or a completed S2.

adjacentBoundaries.internal: User-scoped bootstrap and stable dispatcher, host admission, immutable local releases, enrollment, locking, durable recovery, state-compatibility checks and daemon readiness. Local fixtures exercise source and signed predecessors.

Local exact-asset qualification harness and evidence attestation, publication and discovery wiring, cross-target checks, and source-mode ARM regression. S3 consumes S1 signing and S2 lifecycle contracts.

nonFunctional.security: A build can never read deployment keys. Signing jobs consume bounded inputs from trusted workflows, never execute candidate files, and bind exact origin and policy. Reject substituted trust roots, unsafe archives, unsupported host or ABI, missing enrolled metadata, replays, and nonmatching process ownership before live mutation. The private state directory and signed installation require no root or system service changes.
nonFunctional.durability: Select a staged immutable release only after verified admission. Persist the floor and recovery record with file and parent-directory durability and use identity-bound process operations. Retain exact signed inputs, predecessor proof and state-compatibility proof for offline retry and recovery.
nonFunctional.observability: Report platform, target, release identity, selected delivery mode and safe recovery status through existing surfaces. Keep trust secrets and absolute evidence details out of user-facing status. Qualification records actual kernel and user-space architecture, virtualization mode and test evidence digests.
nonFunctional.performance: Stage, verify, and check compatibility while the incumbent runs. Downtime begins only at verified drain and ends at candidate readiness or safe recovery. No release tests run in hosted signing workflows.

parameters.purpose: Exact repository, ref, commit, run, attempt, artifact, target, channel and manifest and archive digests

parameters.purpose: Detached evidence-domain signature pinned by protected control

returns.meaning: Validated identity and evidence hashes usable by guarded signing

errors.condition: Missing, failed, duplicate, unexpected or mismatched tests, evidence source, subject, host or applicable predecessor

preconditions: Expected subject comes from trusted artifact retrieval and current protected release control. Trusted signing initiates from protected code with role-separated credentials.

The exact manifest and its qualification-only grant come from trusted signing output. The final signer verifies that grant with the independently pinned qualification key and compares it with the qualification receipt and immutable archive before admitting the final signature.
postconditions: A candidate or build token cannot approve its own evidence. Final signing repeats protected branch/ref authorization and checks exact bytes and all evidence requirements before signing the unchanged manifest.

Under protected serialization, durably bind the release sequence to the exact manifest digest before the final signature is made available. An identical retry may reuse that binding. A lower sequence or a different digest at an already allocated sequence cannot be signed.

dataModelChanges.details: One exact checkout, run attempt and target produces one archive, one bounded build record and one uploaded artifact. The build record declares full ref, version, target, archive basename, digest and bytes, and staged runtime fingerprint. The upload result binds artifact ID to an exact job and attempt. The protected fetch verifies workflow ID, repository and head repository, event, successful run and attempt, ref, commit, target-qualified name, artifact ID, expiry and transport digest or protected archive digest. Reject duplicate or unexpected outer members before streaming only bounded named entries. Records supplied by the candidate never establish authorization.
dataModelChanges.schemaDiff: Linux candidates use daemon-candidate-linux-x64-<lane>-<commit>-<attempt> and insrc-daemon-<version>-linux-x64.tar.gz. Versions and IDs are strictly bounded. Run and artifact IDs are canonical decimal strings. The build job receives no release keys or write token.

dataModelChanges.entity: Linux manifest v1 and detached roles
dataModelChanges.details: One candidate produces one strict versioned UTF-8 Linux manifest with one final lane, channel and sequence. It binds origin, target, candidate archive name, size, digest, runtime fingerprint and host contract. The host baseline carries Ubuntu 24.04 LTS amd64, glibc requirements, verified Node 22.22.1, runtime system library allowlist and pidfd requirement. Qualification and final grants sign the identical raw manifest with role-specific namespace and keys. Development enrollment binds an exact configured full branch ref and repo, using an unambiguous per-ref channel identity. Production lane uses the protected release ref. Mutable download locators supply candidates only. Protected signing maintains one durable sequence ledger per repository, target, final lane and channel scope. Qualification proposes the sequence and never allocates a final release slot. Final authorization commits the sequence binding with immutable compare-and-set semantics. Serializing within a runner is insufficient across jobs, reruns or ref changes.
dataModelChanges.schemaDiff: Manifest max 32 KiB with strict UTF-8, strict fields, duplicate-key rejection and safe positive sequence. SHA-256 is canonical lower hex. Signature is exactly 64 bytes. Archive has bounded verified size and SHA-256. Raw bytes are immutable between qualification and final signing. Compatibility declarations identify the target state and eligible predecessor fingerprints. Only a proved pair can later upgrade.

dataModelChanges.details: One candidate may have multiple qualification attempts. Promotion selects one independently attested complete run or evidence record that maps each required case to its positive result, host profile and evidence digest. Predecessor compatibility proof is a detached section of this record, outside the manifest. It binds candidate and predecessor identities and state contract so the digest of a final manifest never depends on evidence collected by installing that same manifest. The owner proves selected target, subject and predecessor by exact digests. S1 implements parsing and authorization with fixtures. S3 produces the real record. The attestation is an independently signed detached proof for the exact artifact. Production and development consume the same proof format under their respective policy and namespace. S2 reads the applicable proof from authenticated release inputs, independently of the mutable release locator.
dataModelChanges.schemaDiff: QualificationSubject binds the raw manifest digest, archive digest, exact origin, target and channel. Evidence binds unique required case IDs and outcomes, ABI/host profile digest and optional required predecessor proof. The verifier chooses required case IDs from trusted policy.

interactionWithShared.howDetails: Produce and validate one Linux archive and strict authenticated manifest with a pinned host baseline and separate signature roles. Reuse bounded byte verification and safe USTAR staging without relaxing Darwin gates.
Validate protected origin and independently signed qualification evidence against exact immutable candidate and predecessor identities. Live test execution and publication are S3 responsibilities.

errorCases.detection: Verify name, size and digest from a private snapshot and apply bounded USTAR staging and runtime fingerprint checks.
errorCases.userImpact: Operator retrieves the immutable approved asset.

errorCases.detection: Compare signed receipt with required case set, per-case result and exact host, subject and predecessor requirements.
errorCases.response: Block final signing and preserve isolated candidate for inspection.
errorCases.userImpact: Release owner reruns the failed local cases.

errorCases.detection: Compare the protected channel sequence head and existing binding while committing the requested allocation.
errorCases.response: Refuse changed or lower release identities. Permit an exact retry with the existing binding.
errorCases.userImpact: The release owner must qualify a new manifest if the sequence was already bound to another release.

invariantsToPreserve.text: Existing production and development Darwin v1 shape and signature allowlists remain unchanged.
Safe staging accepts only a bounded archive and an exact digest supplied from verified metadata. The stage stays private and cannot escape its parent.

testStrategy.testFramework: Node.js node:test via the repository's existing TypeScript test loader for scripts/__tests__. Run packaging and ABI smoke tests locally on Ubuntu 24.04 amd64. Use controlled fixture keys and protected-run fixtures without production credentials.

testLevels.purpose: Validate metadata, trust envelopes, and archive limits
subjects: Strict manifest fields and branch/channel derivation

testLevels.purpose: Validate build provenance and protected final authorization
subjects: Wrong run attempt or asset target
Required evidence, role separation and separate Darwin coordinates

testLevels.purpose: Demonstrate the locally built archive matches the minimum runtime baseline
subjects: Relocated native binary and addon loading
Signed manifest and verified staged fingerprint
Required daemon, CLI and MCP entrypoints

provingTests: Build from a clean Ubuntu 24.04 amd64 checkout, verify runtime provenance, unpack at a different root with the shared verifier, and load required native modules with the bundled Node.
Verify the Linux broker and shutdown watchdog are packaged and smoke their runtime entry points. Reject foreign ELF objects, excess ABI requirements and missing native dependencies.
Verify both allowed development refs with one configuration-only allowlist change and reject unconfigured or protected-role crossovers.

Prove identical manifest bytes across isolated and final grants. Reject alternate role or key, altered archive, malformed manifest, missing evidence, repeated test IDs, and foreign predecessor or host evidence.
Race final authorization from two runs for the same channel sequence. Verify only one distinct manifest can be signed and its exact retry remains valid after interruption.
Record Darwin and Linux builds with the same version and verify independent artifact lookup by target, workflow/run/attempt and ID.
Reject wrong-GitHub-attempt, wrong artifact ID, candidate from another repo, swapped target, and ambiguous archive ZIP members. Run existing Darwin metadata, candidate and staging regression tests.

migration.stateBefore: The analyzer located independent Darwin release and development manifests and consumers of shared bounded staging. Both legacy manifest readers enforce darwin-arm64. [[c1]] [[c2]]
migration.stateAfter: A Linux x86-64 candidate and signed manifest can be produced and independently qualified using the added target contract. Existing Darwin artifacts continue using their previous verification path, and Linux ARM retains source sync.

migrationSteps.action: Add the Linux-only metadata and signer input contract alongside existing Darwin versions.
Add an isolated Linux x86-64 build and exact-origin verification entry point. Keep production artifact publication gated by S3.
Exercise the new target with local signed fixtures and retain existing Darwin regression coverage.

migration.backwardCompat: No existing asset format, tag, signature, Darwin workflow contract or Linux source entry point changes. The Linux candidate workflow can be disabled without changing existing installations.

alternativesConsidered.name: Dedicated Linux v1 manifest and role-separated signatures
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Use one Linux target format while retaining existing Darwin metadata and local staging.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Add a narrow Linux contract for the exact staged runtime and host baseline. Role-separated Ed25519 signatures authenticate the same manifest bytes for isolated qualification and final use, with origin, role and channel enforced out of band by the trusted verifier.
pros: Existing Mac manifest formats and artifact names remain compatible.
Local qualification can use identical candidate bytes across roles.

alternativesConsidered.name: Separate Linux formats for each channel
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Define one Linux development schema and one Linux production schema.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Use target-specific manifests for both channels, with independent strict parsers and signatures. Keep the shared qualification subject explicit and attach a separate common evidence record to each format.
pros: Channel-specific fields and parser policy are explicit.
cons: Two Linux parsers duplicate ABI checks and make identical qualification and release payload handling harder.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Separate payload formats duplicate the same validation and complicate exact-byte qualification.

sequenceDefinition.narrative: The sequence shows which actor controls the original build identity and when the separate signature grants are available. The final signer authenticates qualification evidence before it signs the same manifest bytes.
